newsitem.title: UK: Whitbread names Thomas new chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Whitbread names Thomas new chief executive.

text.p: British leisure and brewery group Whitbread Plc said on Thursday it had appointed David Thomas as its chief executive designate to take over from Peter Jarvis who is to step down in summer 1997.
Chairman Sir Michael Angus described Thomas as "the company's most experienced retailer", adding "he has been responsible for much of our recent expansion in hotels, eating-out and active leisure".
Analysts expect Thomas to expand further Whitbread's leisure and restaurant business while retaining an interest in brewing.
His appointment is viewed as a natural progression from the Jarvis era which saw Whitbread aggressively transform itself from a brewer to a diversified leisure company.

In 1985/86 37 percent of Whitbread's profits came from retail, 43 percent from beer and 20 percent other drinks. In 1995/96 40 percent of its income came from its managed estate, 28 percent from restaurant and leisure, 18 percent from its pub partnerships and just 14 percent from beer.

"We knew he was going to leave before retirement age although these announcements are always a bit of a surprise when they come. The appointment of David Thomas seems like a natural progression for the company," said John Beaumont, an analyst at Merrill Lynch.

Thomas, who was appointed to the main board in 1991 and took over the restaurant and leisure division in 1992, is credited with accelerating the development of Whitbread's existing brands -- Travel Inn, restaurants TGI Friday's and Beefeater.
He was also the architect of Whitbread's drive into the pub food market through Brewers Fayre.
Thomas worked closely with Jarvis on two landmark deals for the company in August 1995 -- the purchase of sports centres David Lloyd Leisure and 16 Marriot Hotels,

Jarvis, aged 55, has hinted to reporters at recent press conferences he would prefer to leave the company before reaching retirement age in order to pursue outside interests. He is currently a non-executive director of Burton, Rank and Barclays Plc.
